title: Hardware curation and pin recommendation lifecycle for multi‑SKU model profiles
creator: Miguel Torres
description:
Goal: define and implement a reproducible lifecycle for hardware‑specific performance profiles (A100/H100/L40S/MI300) that yields deterministic pin recommendations for model variants and a publishable profile artifact.

Motivation: model onboarding currently yields profiles that drift between calibration runs and across device skus. This leads to noisy pin suggestions and oscillating rollouts for Dedicated/Private customers. We need a clear curation and TTL policy, deterministic signature generation, and a verified publish pipeline so customers can pin with confidence.

Scope:
- Define canonical calibration workload and telemetry to collect (latency P50/P95/P99, tail qps, memory footprint, kv cache hit rates, batch efficiency, variance over warmup).
- Establish per‑sku normalization rules and a cross‑sku comparison metric for deciding safe pinning ranges.
- Implement a signature file format (human readable + cryptographic hash) that encodes model version, commit hash, device sku, compiler flags, quantization profile, and sample distribution.
- Build an automated validation harness that runs calibration on target skus (A100, H100, L40S, MI300) and emits a publishable profile if stability thresholds pass.
- Define auto‑pin heuristics: when to suggest pin, when to force pin for SLA customers, and when to recommend a compatible fallback. Include decay/TTL and deprecation path for old pins.
- Wire profile publication into the existing artifacts pipeline (S3/GCS + metadata index) and surface in Console + SDK as a named profile.

Out of scope: refactoring runtime kernels or inventing new quantization schemes (this ticket will surface gaps to follow‑on tickets).

Deliverables:
1) Calibration harness runbook and canonical workload spec (link to Confluence below).
2) Profile schema + signature spec and RFC.
3) Automation to run scheduled nightly calibrations for each supported sku and push candidate profiles to a staging index.
4) Canary rollout playbook and PR template that includes sample traces, stability deltas, and rollback criteria.
5) Console UI hooks for showing profile age, stability score, and recommended pin action.

References and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Canonical+HW+Calibration+Workload
- Benchmark matrix (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-benchmark-matrix
- Existing stability thresholds doc: internal/ENG-31642 (see dependencies)

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness can run an end‑to‑end profile job for A100/H100/L40S/MI300 and produce the profile json+signature
Profiles include latency distributions (P50/P95/P99), batch efficiency, memory high watermark, and KV cache microstats
Signature files contain deterministic fields and a SHA256 hash; two identical runs on identical infra yield same signature
Auto‑publish pipeline stages: staging -> canary -> published with clear manual approval gate for customer‑facing publish
Console shows profile metadata (sku, model hash, created_at, stability_score) and a single‑click recommend pin action
Pin recommendation logic produces a human‑readable rationale and a risk score; p99 regressions > 10% block auto‑pin
comments: 2025-11-14 — Miguel Torres: Initial investigation complete. Baseline calibration workload defined (50 warmup sequences, 2000 inference requests across seq lengths [32,128,512], 8 batch sizes). Found wide variance on MI300 tail latency after cold start; suspect kernel scheduling differences.

2025-11-18 — Claire Nguyen: Prototype signature schema uploaded to RFC branch. It contains model_git_sha, tokenizer_sha, device_sku, nvcc_flags, quant_profile, workload_id. Need feedback from infra on including driver versions.

2025-11-22 — Priya Shah (SRE): Suggested adding GPU driver and CUDA/cuBLAS/ROCm versions to signature. Also recommended a driver‑compatibility label to mark profiles that are only valid on certain driver ranges.

2025-11-26 — Claire Nguyen: Added validation harness that runs on a 3‑node H100 testbed; results pushed to staging index. Observed consistent 4–6% P95 variance between runs on H100 and L40S for long sequences. Created follow‑up ENG-50124 to investigate kernel launch padding.

2025-12-01 — Miguel Torres: Implemented stability_score calculation (weighted on P99 and batch_efficiency variance). Staging profiles for A100 and H100 passed thresholds; MI300 failed due to intermittent memory reclaim events during GC. Scheduling post‑mortem and next steps documented.
2025-12-02 — Claire Nguyen: Drafted console wire for profile metadata and 'Recommend Pin' CTA. Need product review for wording and guardrails (only show recommend for enterprise customers initially).
notes: We must include a deprecation TTL for published profiles (default 90 days).
Consider exposing a 'compatibility shim' in the runtime to allow soft falls from a pinned variant to a compatible quantized variant when capacity constrained.
Engage Model Onboarding PM for rollout comms and changelog formatting.
risk: Medium — incorrect pin recommendations could cause customer regressions; mitigated by canary gating and manual approval for production publish.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Spec and signature RFC (2 weeks). Phase 2: Calibration harness + nightly jobs (3 weeks). Phase 3: Console surface + canary publish (2 weeks). Follow‑ups: kernel investigations flagged by harness (separate tickets).
estimated_cost: ~3k compute hours across testbeds (A100/H100/L40S/MI300) for initial calibration; will optimize after first pass
owner_notes: Prioritize stability detection heuristics and make signature schema conservative. For early launch only allow recommend_pin for enterprise orgs behind feature flag.
